plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because bidding too high risks overpaying, while bidding too low risks losing the auction to someone who values the item less. Since it is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid slightly below my value to try and win at a reasonable price. I'll bid $13.50.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because any bid above that point risks overpaying, and any bid below risks letting the item go for less than its worth. Since this is round 1 with no history, I will implement this strategy. My value is $34, so 2/3 * $34 = $22.67. I will round this to the nearest tenth.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win with high probability and minimize overpayment, I'll bid slightly above this. Considering the risk aversion, I will bid $33.60.
